classes.name: Oral corticosteroids
classes.description: Systemic oral corticosteroids: prednisone (tablets, solution; Rayos delayed-release appears discontinued), methylprednisolone (Medrol, dose pack), prednisolone (solution, Orapred ODT, Millipred), dexamethasone (tablets, solution, Dexamethasone Intensol, TaperDex/Dxevo/HiDex packs; Hemady 20 mg is labeled for multiple myeloma only, an alternative, never the pick), hydrocortisone (Cortef; Alkindi Sprinkle and Khindivi oral solution for children). Deflazacort (Emflaza) and vamorolone (Agamree) for Duchenne are specialty alternatives only, never the pick. Not budesonide (Entocort, Uceris, Tarpeyo) or inhaled/topical steroids.
classes.plainDescription: Short courses of steroid pills that calm inflammation fast, for flares of asthma, COPD, arthritis, allergies and more.
classes.indication: Inflammatory flares, asthma/COPD exacerbations, autoimmune disease, adrenal insufficiency

preferredAgent.sig: Dose by condition, 5 to 60 mg by mouth daily, with food (label). A common short course for a flare is 40 mg once daily for 5 days (practice, not label text); taper courses longer than 2 to 3 weeks.
preferredAgent.sigShort: 5-60 mg QD; flare often 40 mg x5d
preferredAgent.plainSig: Take with food in the morning, at the dose and for the days your prescriber sets.

paRequired.reason: Preferred brand over generic (BvG) for Duchenne muscular dystrophy only, with PA: neurologist or DMD specialist; DMD confirmed by genetic testing or biopsy; inadequate response of at least 180 days or contraindication to prednisone (UPDL p. 72)
Not preferred: PA required; unmanageable side effects or intolerance of at least 30 days with at least 1 preferred drug, indicated for diagnosis (UPDL p. 72)
Not preferred: PA required, same criteria as Agamree: intolerance of at least 30 days with at least 1 preferred drug indicated for the diagnosis (UPDL p. 72)

records.verificationNote: The UPDL has no systemic oral corticosteroid category. records.verificationNote: Read from the formulary text layer, row by row (each tier digit sits on the same row as its drug name; pypdf gave no x-coordinates for the digits). Formulary sig and quantity limits are as printed; the document prints no sig, so the sig is the label starting dose. Prednisone 10 mg tablet is Tier 1 with no PA; BvsD is a Part B versus Part D review flag, not a PA, so it is not in preferredRestriction (PDG p. 61). Not listed: Rayos, Medrol, Orapred ODT, Millipred, Cortef, TaperDex, Dxevo, HiDex. Hydrocortisone tablets print on p. 54 (in the list's dermatology block) and are cited as printed. [Sonnet check 2026-11-06: tiers and flags re-read in layout (row-aligned) extraction, not flattened text; nonformulary reasons reworded to the front-matter wording; prednisone tablets carry BvsD (Part B vs D review, not PA); dose pack does not; added Rayos and Khindivi as not listed.] [Reused: same national Humana Premier Rx PDP formulary]
